speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether more handicap-accessible car park lots will be provided at HDB and URA-managed car parks to provide for an accessible built environment; and (b) when is the next review on the Code on Accessibility in the Built Environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The number of lots provided in HDB’s car parks is in accordance with the Code.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: URA car parks, which are typically off-street or curbside parking that are not part of a development, also take guidance from the Code for the provision of accessible parking lots.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Just a quick supplementary question for the Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I raised this Parliamentary Question because I have more and more residents coming to me to say that in the places that they go to, for those who are physically immobile, they are finding it sometimes not so easy to find the lots that they have.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Obviously, we do know that more of us are ageing, more of us do need these aids and, therefore, planning parameters do need to change.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I recognise that the next review is next year, in 2023, as the Minister of State just said.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I hope that, in the review, we will do with a more future-back kind of lens because I think this ageing trend is taking place very, very quickly.
